title: Short Stuff: Alternative Libraries
summary: Short Stuff episode hosted by Josh and Chuck on "alternative libraries." Chuck opens with his love of neighborhood Little Free Libraries and a children's book he picked up from one. The hosts cover the origin of Little Free Library: Todd Bowle of Hudson, Wisconsin built a model one-room schoolhouse as a tribute to his mother, a teacher, in 2009; with Rick Brooks they set a goal of 2,508 libraries by end of 2013 (a nod to Andrew Carnegie's public libraries), which was surpassed; by 2022 there were over 150,000 worldwide in 120 countries; Brooks retired in 2014; Margaret Aldrich wrote a Little Free Library book; Bowle died in 2018 of pancreatic cancer after the 75,000th library. Then they discuss the Human Library, created by brothers Ronnie Abergel and Danny Abergel for a festival in Denmark around 2000, where "human books" who are often marginalized (trans people, unhoused people, people of different races) are checked out for conversation. Rules for readers, book depots (mobile libraries), international spread, and corporate events (Microsoft, Eli Lilly) are covered.

segments.title: Opening and neighborhood Little Free Libraries
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck introduce the episode on alternative libraries. Chuck describes the small book-sharing boxes he sees on his neighborhood walks and a book he took for his daughter.

segments.title: Origins of Little Free Library
segments.summary: Chuck explains that Todd Bowle of Hudson, Wisconsin started Little Free Library in 2009 with a model schoolhouse honoring his teacher mother. Josh describes the Carnegie-inspired goal of 2,508 libraries by the end of 2013, which the founders, Bowle and Rick Brooks, exceeded.

segments.title: Growth of Little Free Library and Todd Bowle's legacy
segments.summary: Chuck covers the charter signs, the rapid spread, Brooks's 2014 retirement, Margaret Aldrich's book, and the 2014 Library of Congress Literacy Award. Josh gives the 2022 figure of more than 150,000 libraries in 120 countries. Bowle died in 2018 of pancreatic cancer after the 75,000th library launched; a quote from him is read.

segments.title: Give a book, take a book concept
segments.summary: The hosts recap the give-a-book, take-a-book premise of Little Free Library and joke about donating and spotting the book in the wild.
topics: give a book take a book

segments.title: The Human Library
segments.summary: Brothers Ronnie Abergel and Danny Abergel created the Human Library for a Danish festival around 2000, where marginalized people (trans people, unhoused people, people of different races) are 'checked out' as human books for conversation. Chuck describes its start as a festival with 50 human books over four days and its spread to Asia, Africa, Australia, the Americas and Europe. Josh explains the volunteer vetting process, the 'publishing' step, and reader rules.

segments.title: Corporate Human Library events
segments.summary: Chuck notes companies such as Microsoft and Eli Lilly have hosted human library events with guest speakers, and the hosts joke about skeptical attendees.

segments.title: Book Depots mobile libraries and closing thoughts
segments.summary: Josh describes Book Depots, the mobile Human Library headquartered in Copenhagen that takes books on the road. The hosts wrap up by encouraging support for Little Free Library, the Human Book Project, and all libraries.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck sign off the Short Stuff episode.
